objectClass.notes: One isolated empty architectural assembly reconstructed as a real-time browser environment; no furniture is inferred from references.

reasoning: Simple rectangular silhouette, but near-360 coverage requires four independent inward-facing wall assemblies and stable camera-side culling.
Window opening is geometric: four wall panels, reveal/frame/sill, mullions, four glass panes and exterior backing.
Material fidelity depends on separate deterministic wall, floor and painted-frame PBR channels plus repeated plank geometry.
Existing desk coordinates and camera orbit are authoritative constraints not visible in the reference images.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Exact room dimensions are not measurable; derive a documented proportion from the 12 x 8 desk footprint.
Top view is not perfectly orthographic; use it only for rectangular topology.
Window elevation centers the window while perspective placement is ambiguous; choose a small northward offset and record low confidence.
No ceiling is built because the user requested only window, walls and floor.
Exterior scene and manufacturing wall thickness are undefined; use a pale backing panel and view-supporting recess only.

details.description: One tall rectangular opening cuts the west wall; it must change topology rather than appear as a dark decal.
details.affects: west wall silhouette and negative space

details.description: Deep pale reveal wraps the window opening and catches a broad highlight.
Painted outer frame and sill use real narrow edge relief, not a flat plane.
One vertical and one horizontal painted-wood mullion divide the glazing into four panes.
Four glazing regions show low-roughness pale sky response without detailed exterior scenery.
Wall albedo has very low-contrast broad mottling; it is paint variation, not dirt or directional lighting baked into color.
Fine painted-plaster grain adds shallow normal/height response under grazing light.
Pale baseboard forms a continuous raised band with a narrow top step at every wall-floor junction.
Long parallel wood boards have real narrow dark gaps running along room depth.
Each plank carries longitudinal multi-frequency wood grain aligned with its long axis.
Adjacent planks vary subtly in warm-brown value without a repeating checker pattern.
Window frame and baseboard retain faint directional painted-wood grain beneath a satin finish.
details.affects: painted wood albedo, height and roughness

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The existing desk remains at world origin without scale or position changes, and the room floor top sits just below every desk-leg bottom with no visible gap or penetration.
Four independent inward-facing walls form a rectangular shell; the camera can orbit close to 360 degrees because a wall viewed from outside is back-face culled rather than blocking the desk.
Only the west wall contains one real opening with frame, sill, mullions, four glass panes and a pale exterior backing; north, east and south remain blank.
Floor planks have real seams, deterministic color variation and independent albedo/roughness/height/AO evidence; wall paint and painted wood retain readable low-amplitude relief under grazing light.
Primary, opposite-corner, side and material-close-up renders plus automated structure/resource tests pass without adding another Canvas or persistent room state.

featureGroups.name: Desk-to-room spatial contract
qualityCriteria: Floor height is derived from DESK_MODEL_SPEC leg center and height.
Desk, mat, notebook and sticker hit surface coordinates remain unchanged.
failureModes: desk legs penetrate or float above floor
room integration moves existing interactive objects

featureGroups.name: Rectangular shell and near-360 orbit visibility
qualityCriteria: Four named walls bound a 4:3-like floor footprint.
Every wall uses an inward-facing one-sided surface so camera-side walls cull from outside.
failureModes: near wall permanently obscures desk during orbit

featureGroups.name: West four-pane window assembly
qualityCriteria: A geometric opening is surrounded by separate wall panels.
Frame, sill, one vertical mullion, one horizontal mullion and four inset panes are named parts.
failureModes: window is painted onto a solid wall
window appears on more than one wall

featureGroups.name: Independent procedural PBR surface response
qualityCriteria: Wall, floor and painted wood generate deterministic albedo, roughness, height and AO data independently.
Albedo maps are sRGB while data maps remain linear.
Macro, meso and micro bands remain visible but lower contrast than the desk.
failureModes: albedo reused as a data map
room texture contrast competes with desk

featureGroups.name: Runtime part hierarchy, budgets and disposal
qualityCriteria: Named floor, walls, baseboards and window parts are clickable/explodable from one shared part definition.
root.userData.sculptRuntime, resource metrics and dispose are present.
All owned geometry, materials and textures are released.

visualDeltaChecks: four-wall rectangular topology and blank-wall opening count
floor plank direction, seam rhythm and material response
wall/frame relief under reference-matched and grazing light
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

authoringInstruction: Fill observed object class, complexity reasoning, featureGroups, visualDeltaChecks, and unknowns before generating or implementing ObjectSculptSpec.
